gold.quote: (4) The FOOD shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if READY-TO-EAT, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control;
(B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours:

lookalike.quote: You can keep chilled food out of the fridge for up to 4 hours, then you must throw it away.
(B) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours to 5 °C (41 °F) or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature
All pasteurized milk and milk products, except the following, shall be stored at a temperature of 7°C (45°F) or less and maintained thereat following filling or until further processed:

note: The demo's own excursion. US 4-hour limit for TCS food out of temperature control; the UK 4-hour rule and the 4-hour cooling rule look the same.

gold.quote: On delivery vehicles, the temperature of milk and milk products shall not exceed 7°C (45°F).

lookalike.quote: refrigerated, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be at a temperature of 5 °C (41 °F) or below when received.

setting: a refrigerated truck whose refrigeration unit failed in the US

gold.quote: If a shipper, loader, receiver, or carrier becomes aware of an indication of a possible material failure of temperature control or other conditions that may render the food unsafe during transportation, the food shall not be sold or otherwise distributed

lookalike.quote: a carrier must pre-cool each mechanically refrigerated cold storage compartment as specified by the shipper
the receiver must take steps to adequately assess that the food was not subjected to significant temperature abuse

note: Transport failure: right section of the right rule vs neighbouring duties in the same rule.

setting: transport of quick-frozen food in the EU

gold.quote: The temperature of quick-frozen foodstuffs must be stable and maintained, at all points in the product, at -18 °C or lower, with possibly brief upward fluctuations of no more than 3 °C during transport.

lookalike.quote: Frozen MSM must be wrapped or packaged before storage or transport, must not be stored for more than three months and must be maintained at a temperature of not more than -18 °C during storage and transport.

note: -14 C is 4 C above -18 C, beyond the 3 C transport tolerance.

setting: cold storage of fresh poultry meat in the EU

gold.quote: Meat must attain a temperature of not more than 4 °C before transport, and be maintained at that temperature during transport.
3. As soon as the meat is cut and, where appropriate, packaged, it must be chilled to a temperature of not more than 4 °C.

lookalike.quote: post-mortem inspection must be followed immediately by chilling in the slaughterhouse to ensure a temperature throughout the meat of not more than 3 °C for offal and 7 °C for other meat

note: 6 C passes the red-meat limit (7 C) but fails the poultry limit (4 C): the lookalike gives the wrong decision.

setting: on-farm storage of raw milk collected daily in the EU

gold.quote: Milk must be cooled immediately to not more than 8 °C in the case of daily collection, or not more than 6 °C if collection is not daily;

lookalike.quote: Cooled to 10°C (50°F) or less within four (4) hours after starting the milking operation.

note: 9 C fails the EU 8 C limit but would pass the US 10 C first-stage limit.
